passages.text: “Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: Look to the rock from which you were cut, and to the quarry from which you were hewn.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to people who want to do what is right.
God speaks to people who seek Him.
God says, "Listen to Me."
You pursue righteousness.
You seek the LORD.
Look at the rock where you came from.
Look at the quarry where you were cut out.
You have a strong beginning.
You come from a place that is firm and lasting.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֙יטוּ֙ אֶל־ צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל־ מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave you birth. When I called him, he was but one; then I blessed him and multiplied him.
passages.sermon:
Abraham is your father.
Sarah gave birth to you.
Look to Abraham.
Look to Sarah.
I called Abraham when he was only one person.
I blessed Abraham.
I made Abraham many.
passages.original: הַבִּ֙יטוּ֙ אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אֲבִיכֶ֔ם וְאֶל־ שָׂרָ֖ה תְּחוֹלֶלְכֶ֑ם כִּי־ אֶחָ֣ד קְרָאתִ֔יו וַאֲבָרְכֵ֖הוּ וְאַרְבֵּֽהוּ׃ס

passages.text: For the LORD will comfort Zion and will look with compassion on all her ruins; He will make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and melodious song.
passages.sermon:
The LORD will comfort Zion.
The LORD will show compassion to all the ruins of Zion.
The LORD will make Zion’s wilderness like Eden.
The LORD will make Zion’s desert like the garden of the LORD.
Joy will be found in Zion.
Gladness will be found in Zion.
Thanksgiving will be in Zion.
Songs of praise will be in Zion.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ נִחַ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה צִיּ֗וֹן נִחַם֙ כָּל־ חָרְבֹתֶ֔יהָ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם מִדְבָּרָהּ֙ כְּעֵ֔דֶן וְעַרְבָתָ֖הּ כְּגַן־ יְהוָ֑ה שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יִמָּ֣צֵא בָ֔הּ תּוֹדָ֖ה וְק֥וֹל זִמְרָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Pay attention to Me, My people, and listen to Me, My nation; for a law will go out from Me, and My justice will become a light to the nations; I will bring it about quickly.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God calls His nation to listen to Him.
God says, "Pay attention to Me."
God says, "Listen to Me."
God will send out His law from Himself.
God will make His justice shine as a light for all nations.
God will act quickly to do this.
passages.original: הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ עַמִּ֔י וּלְאוּמִּ֖י אֵלַ֣י הַאֲזִ֑ינוּ כִּ֤י תוֹרָה֙ מֵאִתִּ֣י תֵצֵ֔א וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔י לְא֥וֹר עַמִּ֖ים אַרְגִּֽיעַ׃

passages.text: My righteousness draws near, My salvation is on the way, and My arms will bring justice to the nations. The islands will look for Me and wait in hope for My arm.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is righteous.
The LORD’s righteousness is coming soon.
The LORD brings salvation.
Salvation is on the way.
The LORD’s power will judge the nations.
The LORD’s arm will bring justice to all peoples.
Distant lands will look to the LORD.
The islands will hope in the LORD.
They will wait for the LORD’s power.
passages.original: קָר֤וֹב צִדְקִי֙ יָצָ֣א יִשְׁעִ֔י וּזְרֹעַ֖י עַמִּ֣ים יִשְׁפֹּ֑טוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֣ים יְקַוּ֔וּ וְאֶל־ זְרֹעִ֖י יְיַחֵלֽוּן׃

passages.text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth below; for the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its people will die like gnats. But My salvation will last forever, and My righteousness will never fail.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God tells them to look up at the heavens.
God tells them to look down at the earth below.
The heavens will disappear like smoke.
The earth will wear out like old clothes.
The people living on the earth will die like small insects.
God’s salvation will last forever.
God’s righteousness will never end.
passages.original: שְׂאוּ֩ לַשָּׁמַ֨יִם עֵֽינֵיכֶ֜ם וְֽהַבִּ֧יטוּ אֶל־ הָאָ֣רֶץ מִתַּ֗חַת כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֜יִם כֶּעָשָׁ֤ן נִמְלָ֙חוּ֙ וְהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ כַּבֶּ֣גֶד תִּבְלֶ֔ה וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כְּמוֹ־ כֵ֣ן יְמוּת֑וּן וִישֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לֹ֥א תֵחָֽת׃ס

passages.text: Listen to Me, you who know what is right, you people with My law in your hearts: Do not fear the scorn of men; do not be broken by their insults.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to people who know what is right.
These people have God's law in their hearts.
God says, "Listen to Me."
Do not fear when people scorn you.
Do not be broken by their insults.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ יֹ֣דְעֵי צֶ֔דֶק עַ֖ם תּוֹרָתִ֣י בְלִבָּ֑ם אַל־ תִּֽירְאוּ֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת אֱנ֔וֹשׁ וּמִגִּדֻּפֹתָ֖ם אַל־ תֵּחָֽתּוּ׃

passages.text: For the moth will devour them like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool. But My righteousness will last forever, My salvation through all generations.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says some things do not last.
A moth eats a garment.
A worm eats wool.
These things are destroyed.
But God’s righteousness will last forever.
God’s salvation will remain through all generations.
passages.original: כִּ֤י כַבֶּ֙גֶד֙ יֹאכְלֵ֣ם עָ֔שׁ וְכַצֶּ֖מֶר יֹאכְלֵ֣ם סָ֑ס וְצִדְקָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וִישׁוּעָתִ֖י לְד֥וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD. Wake up as in days past, as in generations of old. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced through the dragon?
passages.sermon:
The arm of the LORD is strong.
The arm of the LORD saves His people.
Wake up, arm of the LORD.
Put on your strength.
Act with power.
Act as you did long ago.
Act as you did in ancient generations.
You cut Rahab to pieces.
You defeated the dragon.
You showed your might in the past.
Show your might again.
passages.original: עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי־ עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה ע֚וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי קֶ֔דֶם דֹּר֖וֹת עוֹלָמִ֑ים הֲל֥וֹא אַתְּ־ הִ֛יא הַמַּחְצֶ֥בֶת רַ֖הַב מְחוֹלֶ֥לֶת תַּנִּֽין׃

passages.text: Was it not You who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made a road in the depths of the sea for the redeemed to cross over?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God has great power.
God dried up the sea.
God dried up the waters of the great deep.
God made a road in the depths of the sea.
God made this road so the redeemed could cross over.
passages.original: הֲל֤וֹא אַתְּ־ הִיא֙ הַמַּחֲרֶ֣בֶת יָ֔ם מֵ֖י תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֑ה הַשָּׂ֙מָה֙ מַֽעֲמַקֵּי־ יָ֔ם דֶּ֖רֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֥ר גְּאוּלִֽים׃

passages.text: So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
passages.sermon:
The LORD redeems His people.
The redeemed people will return.
They will come to Zion.
They will sing as they come.
Everlasting joy will be on their heads.
Gladness will come to them.
Joy will come to them.
Sorrow will leave them.
Sighing will leave them.
passages.original: וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשׁוּב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־ רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂיג֔וּן נָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “I, even I, am He who comforts you. Why should you be afraid of mortal man, of a son of man who withers like grass?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is your Maker.
The LORD says, "I am the one who comforts you."
I alone give you comfort.
Do not fear people.
People are mortal.
Every person will die.
A human being is like grass.
Grass withers and dies.
People also fade away.
Do not be afraid of them.
passages.original: אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם מִֽי־ אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמ֔וּת וּמִבֶּן־ אָדָ֖ם חָצִ֥יר יִנָּתֵֽן׃

passages.text: But you have forgotten the LORD, your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in terror all day long because of the fury of the oppressor who is bent on destruction. But where is the fury of the oppressor?
passages.sermon:
You have forgotten the LORD.
The LORD is your Maker.
The LORD stretched out the heavens.
The LORD laid the foundations of the earth.
You live in fear all day.
You fear the anger of the oppressor.
The oppressor is determined to destroy.
But where is the oppressor’s fury?
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֞ח יְהוָ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ נוֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַיִם֮ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָרֶץ֒ וַתְּפַחֵ֨ד תָּמִ֜יד כָּל־ הַיּ֗וֹם מִפְּנֵי֙ חֲמַ֣ת הַמֵּצִ֔יק כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר כּוֹנֵ֖ן לְהַשְׁחִ֑ית וְאַיֵּ֖ה חֲמַ֥ת הַמֵּצִֽיק׃

passages.text: The captive will soon be freed; he will not die in the dungeon, and his bread will not be lacking.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He promises freedom to the captive.
The captive will soon be released.
He will not die in the dungeon.
He will have enough bread.
God will provide for him.
passages.original: מִהַ֥ר צֹעֶ֖ה לְהִפָּתֵ֑חַ וְלֹא־ יָמ֣וּת לַשַּׁ֔חַת וְלֹ֥א יֶחְסַ֖ר לַחְמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For I am the LORD your God who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar— the LORD of Hosts is His name.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He stirs up the sea.
The waves of the sea roar because of Him.
His name is the LORD of Hosts.
passages.original: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ רֹגַ֣ע הַיָּ֔ם וַיֶּהֱמ֖וּ גַּלָּ֑יו יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I have put My words in your mouth, and covered you with the shadow of My hand, to establish the heavens, to found the earth, and to say to Zion, ‘You are My people.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD puts His words in your mouth.
The LORD covers you with the shadow of His hand.
The LORD does this to establish the heavens.
The LORD does this to found the earth.
The LORD says to Zion, “You are My people.”
passages.original: וָאָשִׂ֤ים דְּבָרַי֙ בְּפִ֔יךָ וּבְצֵ֥ל יָדִ֖י כִּסִּיתִ֑יךָ לִנְטֹ֤עַ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְלִיסֹ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ וְלֵאמֹ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן עַמִּי־ אָֽתָּה׃ס

passages.text: Awake, awake! Rise up, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His fury; you who have drained the goblet to the dregs— the cup that makes men stagger.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem, you are the city of God’s people.
You have suffered greatly.
You drank the cup of God’s anger.
God gave you this cup with His own hand.
You drank the cup of His fury.
You drained the cup completely.
This cup makes people stagger.
You have felt the full force of God’s wrath.
Now, wake up.
Wake up again.
Stand up, Jerusalem.
passages.original: הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י ק֚וּמִי יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁתִ֛ית מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ כּ֣וֹס חֲמָת֑וֹ אֶת־ קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֛ה שָׁתִ֖ית מָצִֽית׃

passages.text: Among all the sons she bore, there is no one to guide her; among all the sons she brought up, there is no one to take her hand.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is like a mother.
She has many sons.
She gave birth to many children.
None of her sons guide her.
She raised many children.
None of her sons take her hand.
passages.original: אֵין־ מְנַהֵ֣ל לָ֔הּ מִכָּל־ בָּנִ֖ים יָלָ֑דָה וְאֵ֤ין מַחֲזִיק֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ מִכָּל־ בָּנִ֖ים גִּדֵּֽלָה׃

passages.text: These pairs have befallen you: devastation and destruction, famine and sword. Who will grieve for you? Who can comfort you?
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem has suffered greatly.
She has experienced two pairs of disasters.
The first pair is devastation and destruction.
The second pair is famine and sword.
No one grieves for her.
No one can comfort her.
passages.original: שְׁתַּ֤יִם הֵ֙נָּה֙ קֹֽרְאֹתַ֔יִךְ מִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑ךְ הַשֹּׁ֧ד וְהַשֶּׁ֛בֶר וְהָרָעָ֥ב וְהַחֶ֖רֶב מִ֥י אֲנַחֲמֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street, like an antelope in a net. They are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
passages.sermon:
Your sons have fainted.
They lie at the head of every street.
They are like an antelope caught in a net.
They are full of the LORD’s wrath.
They have received the rebuke of your God.
passages.original: בָּנַ֜יִךְ עֻלְּפ֥וּ שָׁכְב֛וּ בְּרֹ֥אשׁ כָּל־ חוּצ֖וֹת כְּת֣וֹא מִכְמָ֑ר הַֽמְלֵאִ֥ים חֲמַת־ יְהוָ֖ה גַּעֲרַ֥ת אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to you now.
You are afflicted.
You are suffering.
You are like someone who is drunk.
You are not drunk from wine.
Listen to this message.
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְעִי־ נָ֥א זֹ֖את עֲנִיָּ֑ה וּשְׁכֻרַ֖ת וְלֹ֥א מִיָּֽיִן׃ס

passages.text: Thus says your Lord, the LORD, even your God, who defends His people: “See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering. From that goblet, the cup of My fury, you will never drink again.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your Lord and your God.
The LORD defends His people.
The LORD says this to you.
I have taken the cup of staggering from your hand.
This cup is the goblet of My fury.
You will never drink from it again.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה וֵאלֹהַ֙יִךְ֙ יָרִ֣יב עַמּ֔וֹ הִנֵּ֥ה לָקַ֛חְתִּי מִיָּדֵ֖ךְ אֶת־ כּ֣וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֑ה אֶת־ קֻבַּ֙עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס חֲמָתִ֔י לֹא־ תוֹסִ֥יפִי לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: I will place it in the hands of your tormentors, who told you: ‘Lie down, so we can walk over you,’ so that you made your back like the ground, like a street to be traversed.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people, Israel.
God promises to act for them.
God says, “I will take the cup of My anger from you.
I will give this cup to your tormentors.
These tormentors hurt you.
They said to you, ‘Lie down, so we can walk over you.’
You obeyed them.
You made your back like the ground.
You became like a street for people to walk on.”
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֙יהָ֙ בְּיַד־ מוֹגַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־ אָמְר֥וּ לְנַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ שְׁחִ֣י וְנַעֲבֹ֑רָה וַתָּשִׂ֤ימִי כָאָ֙רֶץ֙ גֵּוֵ֔ךְ וְכַח֖וּץ לַעֹבְרִֽים׃ס
